issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies numberOfInscribedStudents as an int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as a long. This mismatch is structural and causes downstream problems: the solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns int while adding an int and a long (resulting in long), which is a compile-time type error. Students following the UML or the template will be confused which numeric type to use and may encounter compilation failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the numeric types consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Option A: change numberOfInscribedStudents in the solution to int (update its declaration, getter, setter, and any arithmetic). Option B: update the UML and all method signatures/returns to use long for total student counts (change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long and update related code). Ensure template TODOs and example usages match the chosen type so students have a consistent specification to implement.
